title: IOF Framework Catalogue
description: Machine-readable catalogue of the Interoperability Framework (IOF) for Digital Asset Securities (DTCC, Clearstream, Euroclear, BCG — February 2026). Authoritative resolution target for IOF ids referenced from BPO property records via identifiers.external_refs.iof. This JSON Schema fixes the file SHAPE; internal integrity (id uniqueness across foundations ∪ building_blocks, building_block.foundation closure into foundations) is enforced by schema/validate_refs.py. The Step 3 validator additions further enforce cross-walk closure (every external_refs.iof[].id resolves into building_blocks[]) AND bidirectional scope-link consistency (out-of-scope blocks must carry zero cross-walk links; behavioural blocks must carry at least one) so the `scope` field cannot drift out of sync with the actual links.

description.description: One-line paraphrased description in our own words. Verbatim content from the white paper is limited to the foundation/building-block titles.

enablers.description: The IOF's three cross-cutting enablers (§3.5 of the white paper). A block may carry more than one when its content spans dimensions.

scope.description: Behavioural-test verdict, recorded in the framework data so it is durable and machine-enforceable. `behavioural` blocks are those a smart-contract or ledger system can be proven to satisfy and so admit cross-walking to BPO properties; `out-of-scope` blocks describe legal, regulatory, governance, data-harmonization, operational, or SLA concerns and must carry zero BPO cross-walk links. The bidirectional scope-link consistency check (Step 3 of the IOF integration) enforces this.
